body:
"Near-certain profit" assumes the market is a puzzle with a correct answer. The data describes something else: a lottery-like distribution of outcomes in which skill moves the odds but cannot remove the variance. Bessembinder's US study found that of nearly 26,000 stocks, **just 1,092 companies (4.3%) accounted for all $35 trillion of net wealth creation**. The other 96% collectively matched T-bills ([ASU W.P. Carey](https://wpcarey.asu.edu/department-finance/faculty-research/do-stocks-outperform-treasury-bills)). The global follow-up covered 64,000+ stocks from 1990 to 2020 and found that **about 2.4% of firms created all net shareholder wealth**. In the same study, 57.4% of non-US stocks underperformed T-bills ([Morningstar AU](https://www.morningstar.com.au/stocks/only-2-4-of-companies-deliver-all-net-shareholder-wealth); [ASU](https://wpcarey.asu.edu/department-finance/faculty-research/do-stocks-outperform-treasury-bills)). Motilal Oswal's 2014 100x study found about **47 stocks that did 100x out of a universe of roughly 3,500**, taking about 12 years on average ([Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/interview/how-to-spot-a-100-bagger-744)). Raamdeo Agrawal, whose firm ran that study, says plainly that "100X is a rare phenomenon" ([Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/markets/interview/value-investors-do-not-talk-or-focus-too-much-on-growth-2482)).

Active trading is worse. SEBI found that **93% of about 1.13 crore individual F&O traders lost money over FY22–24, with aggregate losses above ₹1.8 lakh crore** ([News On Air](https://www.newsonair.gov.in/sebi-study-reveals-individual-traders-face-severe-losses-in-equity-fo-segment)). In FY25, 91% lost money and net losses rose 41% to ₹1,05,603 crore ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/net-losses-of-traders-in-fo-widens-in-fy25-sebi-study-125070701221_1.html)). The FY26 study reported 87.7% losers, and **82.1% were losing even before transaction costs** ([Finnovate](https://www.finnovate.in/learn/blog/sebi-fno-trader-losses-fy26-individual-derivatives); [Open Magazine](https://openthemagazine.com/business/sebi-fo-loss-study-explained-why-9-in-10-retail-traders-lost-91685-crore-in-fy26)). That last figure means the problem is not only costs: most of these traders have no edge at all. Studies of other markets agree. **97% of Brazilians who persisted at day trading for 300+ days lost money** ([IDEAS/RePEc](https://ideas.repec.org/p/fgv/eesptd/525.html)). In Taiwan, **fewer than 1% of day traders earned predictable abnormal returns net of fees** ([Barber, Lee, Liu & Odean](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/finmar/v18y2014icp1-24.html)). Professionals do not escape the arithmetic either. SPIVA India Year-End 2025 reports that a majority of active funds in every category underperformed over the decade ([S&P SPIVA](https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/spiva/article/spiva-india-year-end-2025/)).

body:
**Ashish Kacholia**
- He focuses on small and microcaps and takes a "buying a business" approach. He assesses management's integrity, potential and capability, looks for moats and generally buys and holds. He rarely gives interviews. — [Noiseless Trader](https://thenoiselesstrader.beehiiv.com/p/beyond-the-headlines-the-low-profile-strategy-of-ashish-kacholia); [Kotak Securities](https://www.kotaksecurities.com/investing-guide/articles/cloning-the-superstar-of-india) (commentary)

**Basant Maheshwari (*The Thoughtful Investor*)**
- He looks for predictable earnings streams in sectors with strong tailwinds. The book covers both creating and retaining wealth. He has said "No fixed rules here." — [PMS AIF World](https://www.pmsaifworld.com/?p=6444); [Moneyexcel](https://moneyexcel.com/basant-maheshwari-investment-strategy-advice/) (commentary)
- He is widely associated with growth investing and with avoiding PSUs and commodity businesses [unverified].

**Porinju Veliyath (Equity Intelligence)**
- His focus is undervalued small and mid caps. He says "all sensible investing is value investing." He is described as a high-risk contrarian. — [inkl/Equity Intelligence profile](https://www.inkl.com/news/meet-the-risky-investor-equity-intelligence-s-porinju-veliyath); [Groww](https://groww.in/blog/successful-investors-indian-stock-market/) (commentary)

**Dolly Khanna**
- Her husband Rajiv Khanna manages the portfolio. It holds lesser-known, under-the-radar small caps, often in unglamorous manufacturing, chemicals and sugar, with strengthening fundamentals, and is classified as growth style. — [Pocketful](https://www.pocketful.in/blog/top-investors-in-india-and-their-portfolios); [Alice Blue](https://aliceblueonline.com/blog/hindi/porinju-v-veliyath-portfolio-vs-dolly-khanna-portfolio-hindi) (commentary)

**Rakesh Jhunjhunwala (d. 2022)**
- No primary source for a formal checklist was found in this session. Widely attributed themes [unverified] include:
  - a long-term "India growth story" conviction
  - a mix of trading and investing
  - big concentrated bets such as Titan, CRISIL and Lupin
  - management quality first
  - "buy right, sit tight" (more correctly Motilal's phrase)
title: fundamental_frameworks › Cited Findings

body:
- **Decomposition (my estimate, approximate):** From the FY17 trough at about ₹110 to about ₹4,200 is roughly 38x in price. PAT grew from ₹80 cr to ₹602 cr, about 7.5x. Assuming about 13.3–13.4 crore shares **[UNVERIFIED share count]**, market cap went from about ₹1,500 cr to about ₹56,000 cr. That implies trailing P/E rerated from about 18–19x to about 90x+, roughly a 5x multiple expansion. **About 7.5x earnings × about 5x rerating ≈ 38x.** This is the classic "twin engine" (Mayer) or "double whammy" pattern: a low-multiple, levered, out-of-favour company becomes a high-multiple premium consumer brand.
- **The signal that existed early (2016–17):** (a) Prestige & Above volumes growing while regular brands stagnated; (b) management guiding to debt reduction with no new big capex; (c) a raw-material (ENA/grain) cost downcycle reversing; (d) the USL/Diageo turmoil shifting the leader from volume to margin and cutting promotions and leaving shelf space for challengers **[UNVERIFIED as a documented contemporaneous thesis]**; (e) new luxury launches (Rampur single malt, about 2016; Jaisalmer gin; Royal Ranthambore whisky, about 2020) **[launch years UNVERIFIED]**.
- **What a 2008 buyer actually experienced:** a fall from ₹191 to ₹50 in 2008 (−74%), then 8 years range-bound at ₹75–190 before the move. Even a correct thesis required extreme patience and tolerance for opportunity cost. A good lesson in timing versus thesis.
- A user correction is needed: "120 → 4600" is achievable on a 2010–2016 entry, but the trigger was a **2016–17 business inflection (deleveraging + premium mix)** and not a 2008 competitor event.
title: multibagger_case_studies › Inferences

body:
1. **Start-of-production and plant dates slip 1–2 quarters.** Endurance: dual-channel ABS 13 months, ABS lines about 2 quarters, Chennai brakes 2 quarters. Sansera: ADS hangar 1 quarter. Happy Forgings: 4,000-t press 1 quarter. Uniparts: Mexico and the fire rebuild (pilot). OEM validation and customer clearance are the usual stated reasons. **Base case for any auto-component SOP date: about one quarter late.** Note that 46% is the median capacity delivery here; T&D's was 36%.
2. **The government's ABS-mandate guidelines** (not yet notified in Nov-26) delayed brake-capacity timing. This hit Endurance directly and is a sector-level factor.
3. **Margin pressure in H1 FY27 from West Asia–linked steel, copper and aluminium prices and freight** was named by Sona, Endurance, Happy Forgings and Uniparts. Margin *bands* were mostly held. Sona openly lowered its band to 23%.
4. **Capex forecasts are revised upward mid-year** at Sansera (FY26 400 → 510 cr; FY27 510 → 800), Endurance (FY27 "much below 800" → 1,100) and Happy Forgings (FY26 ~300 → 460). This is growth capex for new orders. Score it as a forecasting miss, but don't read it as distress.
